mainTopic: The מן (who ate it, why daily, how high it piled) and the five עינויים of יום הכיפורים
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a דרשה on 'לחם אבירים אכל איש': the 'איש' is יהושע, linked by an exact match of the word 'איש', and not משה ('והאיש'). Next, רבי שמעון בן יוחי explains with a משל of a king and his son why the מן fell every day: so ישראל would turn to their Father in heaven daily. Two more reasons follow: so it could be eaten hot, and so it would not have to be carried on journeys. רבי אלעזר המודעי then claims the מן piled up sixty אמות high. He proves it from the flood: 'windows of heaven' gave fifteen אמות, and 'doors of heaven' are four times bigger. A ברייתא of איסי בן יהודה adds that kings of East and West could see the מן, and אביי learns from 'כוסי רויה' that דוד's cup holds 221 לוג. The גמרא then returns to the משנה of יום הכיפורים: רב חסדא matches five עינויים to five verses, and drinking counts under eating. ריש לקיש's proof from תירוש is rejected. רב אחא בר יעקב's proof from שכר is then challenged by the case of an intoxicating fig, and that discussion continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The 'man' in the verse is יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The 'איש' who ate angel-bread is יהושע, who received מן equal to the amount of all ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is יהושע, for whom מן fell in an amount equal to all of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues explaining the פסוק 'לחם אבירים אכל איש' and says the 'איש' is יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While משה was on הר סיני for forty days, יהושע waited at the foot of the mountain, away from the camp. מן still fell for him there, and it was as much as fell for the whole nation. So the פסוק is read as 'one man ate a huge portion of angel-bread.'

keyTerms.meaning: equal to the amount for all of ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the middle of a longer דרשה from the previous עמוד. The פסוק being explained is 'לחם אבירים אכל איש' (תהלים ע״ח:כ״ה), and this is one more reading of the word 'איש'.

phrases.english: This is Joshua
for whom manna fell
phrases.notes: While he waited for Moses at Sinai

phrases.english: equal to all of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁיָּרַד לוֹ מָן כְּנֶגֶד כׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous עמוד's interpretation of 'לחם אבירים אכל איש'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'איש' in the פסוק is יהושע, who received מן equal to all of ישראל.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'man' used for יהושע
steps.stepSummary: A גזרה שוה: 'איש' here matches 'איש' in the פסוק that calls יהושע 'איש אשר רוח בו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says 'איש' here, and it says 'איש' there: 'Take for yourself יהושע בן נון, a man (איש) who has spirit in him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that 'איש' means יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word 'איש' appears in our פסוק and in במדבר כ״ז:י״ח, where it describes יהושע. A matching word links the two פסוקים, so the 'איש' in our פסוק is also יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: a link between two פסוקים through a shared word

phrases.english: Here it is written 'man,'
and there it is written:
'Take for yourself Joshua son of Nun,
a man who has spirit in him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'איש' who ate angel-bread is יהושע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר כ״ז:י״ח, 'קח לך את יהושע בן נון איש אשר רוח בו', linked by the word 'איש'.

steps.title: Why not say it means משה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: משה is also called 'איש', so maybe the פסוק refers to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is משה, since it is written: 'And the man (והאיש) משה was very humble.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof: משה is also described with the word 'איש'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a shared word is enough, then משה, who is called 'האיש' in במדבר י״ב:ג׳, could just as well be the 'איש' in our פסוק. So the proof for יהושע seems weak.

phrases.english: But say it is Moses,
as it is written:
'And the man Moses was very humble'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the גזרה שוה of step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה is also called 'איש', so the same kind of link could point to משה instead.

steps.title: Only an exact word match counts
steps.stepSummary: We link 'איש' to 'איש', but not 'איש' to 'והאיש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: We compare 'איש' to 'איש', but we do not compare 'איש' to 'והאיש'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the match to יהושע is exact, while the match to משה is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our פסוק says just 'איש', and the יהושע פסוק also says just 'איש'. The משה פסוק says 'והאיש' ('and the man'), which is a different form. An exact word match is stronger, so יהושע wins.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'איש' who ate angel-bread is יהושע, because his פסוק uses the exact same word 'איש'. משה's פסוק says 'והאיש', which is not an exact match.

phrases.english: We derive 'man' from 'man,'
but we do not derive 'man' from 'and the man.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise wording: only an identical word form makes the link.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any use of 'איש' could make the link, so it might be משה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the identical form 'איש' links, so it is יהושע and not משה ('והאיש').

steps.title: Why didn't the manna fall once a year?
steps.stepSummary: The students of רבי שמעון בן יוחי ask why the מן came daily instead of once a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבי שמעון בן יוחי: Why didn't the מן fall for ישראל once a year?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic about the מן with a question from רבי שמעון בן יוחי's students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It would seem easier to give a whole year's supply at once. The students want to know why ה׳ chose to send it day by day.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי שמעון בר יוחאי, a תנא

phrases.english: His students asked
Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא יָרַד לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מָן
phrases.english: Why did the manna not fall for Israel
once a year?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new אגדה about the מן, related by topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the מן fell daily and not as a yearly supply.

steps.title: Parable of the king and his only son
steps.stepSummary: A king who gave his son a yearly allowance saw him once a year, so he switched to a daily allowance and saw him every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I will give you a parable. What is this like? Like a human king who has one son. He gave him his food once a year, and the son came to see his father only once a year. So the king started giving him food every day, and the son came to see his father every day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי begins his answer with a משל. This sets up the lesson that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the son got everything at once, he had no reason to visit. Once his food came daily, he needed his father daily, so he came every day. The king's goal was a close relationship, not just feeding the son.

keyTerms.meaning: I will give you a parable

phrases.english: He said to them:
I will give you a parable:
What is this like?
To a king of flesh and blood
who has one son,
he set his food allowance
once a year,
and he would not greet his father
except once a year.
So he arose and set his food every day,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה מַקְבִּיל פְּנֵי אָבִיו כׇּל יוֹם.
phrases.english: and he would greet his father every day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: אֶמְשׁוֹל לָכֶם מָשָׁל: לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A משל: daily food creates a daily relationship between father and son.

steps.title: The lesson: daily worry led to daily prayer
steps.stepSummary: A father of several children worried each day that the מן might not come, so everyone turned their hearts to ה׳ every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too with ישראל: someone with four or five children would worry and say, 'Maybe the מן won't fall tomorrow, and they will all die of hunger.' So they all turned their hearts to their Father in heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי applies the משל to ישראל in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the מן came only one day at a time, each parent depended on ה׳ again every day. That daily worry made the whole nation turn to their Father in heaven every day, like the son who visited the king daily.
steps.whatToRemember: The first reason the מן fell daily: so ישראל would depend on ה׳ and turn their hearts to Him every day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a basic idea about אמונה and תפילה: daily dependence keeps a person close to ה׳.

phrases.english: So too Israel:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה בָּנִים
phrases.english: one who had four or five children
would worry and say:
Perhaps manna will not fall tomorrow,
and they will all die of hunger,
so they all directed their hearts
to their Father in heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משל of step 6 to ישראל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מן fell daily so that ישראל would turn their hearts to ה׳ every day.

steps.title: Another reason: to eat it hot
steps.stepSummary: A second reason: daily מן could be eaten fresh and hot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: so that they could eat it while it was hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to why the מן fell daily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is practical, not spiritual. A yearly supply would be old by the time it was eaten. Daily מן was always fresh and warm.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
so that they would eat it while it was hot.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלִין אוֹתוֹ כְּשֶׁהוּא חַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מן fell daily so it could be eaten hot and fresh.

steps.title: Another reason: not to carry it while traveling
steps.stepSummary: A third reason: a year's supply would be a heavy burden on their journeys.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: because of the burden of carrying it on the road.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer to why the מן fell daily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישראל moved from place to place in the מדבר. Carrying a whole year of food would be very hard, so the מן fell fresh wherever they were.
steps.whatToRemember: Three reasons the מן fell daily: (1) to keep ישראל turning to ה׳ every day, (2) so it could be eaten hot, (3) so they would not have to carry it on their travels.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
because of the burden of the journey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third answer to the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מן fell daily so they would not have to carry a large supply on their travels.

steps.title: The manna was sixty cubits high
steps.stepSummary: While the sages are learning the section of the מן, רבי אלעזר המודעי states that the מן was sixty אמות high.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once, רבי טרפון, רבי ישמעאל, and the זקנים were sitting and learning the section of the מן, and רבי אלעזר המודעי was sitting with them. רבי אלעזר המודעי spoke up and said: The מן that fell for ישראל was sixty אמות high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a group of sages learning together. In the story, רבי אלעזר המודעי makes a surprising claim about how high the מן piled up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a bold statement given with no source yet. The rest of the section will challenge it and then explain where it comes from. Keep the number sixty in mind, because the whole calculation builds back to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah section about the manna

phrases.english: It once happened that Rabbi Tarfon
and Rabbi Yishmael and the Elders
were sitting and learning the passage of the manna,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַמּוֹדָעִי יוֹשֵׁב בֵּינֵיהֶן.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i was sitting among them.
Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i spoke up and said:
The manna that fell for Israel
was sixty cubits high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reasons why the מן fell daily to a new teaching about how much מן fell.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מן that fell for ישראל piled up sixty אמות high.

steps.title: רבי טרפון objects that this has no basis
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון rebukes רבי אלעזר המודעי for making up teachings without a source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said to him: מודעי, how long will you keep piling up words and bringing them to us?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון challenges the sixty-אמות claim. He suggests it is just made-up talk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection is not about the math. It is about the source: where in the Torah does this come from? This forces רבי אלעזר המודעי to show that his claim is built on a verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Piling up words, i.e., saying things without basis

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said to him: Moda'i,
how long will you keep piling up words
and bringing them upon us!

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹדָעִי, עַד מָתַי אַתָּה מְגַבֵּב דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the statement of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר המודעי's claim that the מן was sixty אמות high
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The claim has no visible source in the Torah, so it looks invented.

steps.title: I am expounding a verse about the flood
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר המודעי answers that his claim comes from a verse, and he begins with the flood verse about fifteen אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי, I am expounding a verse: 'Fifteen אמות above did the waters prevail, and the mountains were covered.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר המודעי defends himself by saying his claim is built on a פסוק. He starts with the verse about the מבול. This is the first building block of his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not mention the מן yet. He first needs to establish exactly how high the flood waters were. He will then compare the מן to the flood.

phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi,
I am expounding a verse:
"Fifteen cubits above
did the waters prevail, and the mountains were covered" (Genesis 7:20)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי טרפון's challenge by pointing to a verse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The claim is derived from verses, starting with the flood verse.

steps.title: The water cannot be fifteen cubits above every kind of ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר המודעי rejects reading the verse as fifteen אמות above every type of ground, because water cannot stand in layers and the ark could not sail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could it mean fifteen אמות in the valley, fifteen in the lowland, and fifteen on the mountains? Does water stand in rows, at different heights? And besides, how could the תיבה travel?
steps.whatsHappening: He rules out a mistaken way to read the verse. The water was not fifteen אמות above each patch of land at different heights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water levels itself out, so it cannot be higher over mountains and lower over valleys. A tilted, step-shaped surface would also make it impossible for the תיבה to float along. This clears the way for the correct reading.
steps.confusionAlert: These questions are not attacking רבי אלעזר המודעי. He is asking them himself, to knock out a wrong reading of the verse before giving the right one.

phrases.english: Could it be fifteen cubits in the valley,
(fifteen in the lowland,)
and fifteen on the mountains?
Does water stand in rows, at different levels?!
And furthermore: how could the Ark travel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a possible reading of the verse quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the verse as fifteen אמות above each local terrain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water cannot rest at uneven heights, and an uneven surface would stop the תיבה from moving.

steps.title: The water first rose to the mountain tops, then fifteen more
steps.stepSummary: The correct reading: the deep burst open until the water was level with the mountains, and then it rose fifteen אמות above them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, all the springs of the great deep burst open until the water reached the level of the mountains, and after that 'fifteen אמות above did the waters prevail.'
steps.whatsHappening: He gives the right reading of the verse. The fifteen אמות are measured above the mountain tops, after the whole world was already flooded up to that level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fifteen אמות were the extra height the rain added over a flat, level surface. It was not uneven height over different ground. This gives a clean measure for the flood that came through the 'windows of heaven,' which will now be compared to the מן.

phrases.english: Rather: were broken open
all the fountains of the great deep
until the water was level with the mountains,
and then "fifteen cubits
above did the waters prevail."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, נִבְקְעוּ כׇּל מַעְיְנוֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading rejected in step 13 with the correct one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fifteen אמות above each kind of ground
steps.terutzMaskana: The water first leveled with the mountains, then the rain added fifteen אמות above them.

steps.title: Goodness is greater than punishment: windows versus doors
steps.stepSummary: God's measure of goodness is greater than His measure of punishment. The flood came through 'windows of heaven,' but the מן came through 'doors of heaven.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Which measure is greater, God's goodness or His punishment? You must say goodness is greater than punishment. About punishment the Torah says: 'And the windows of heaven were opened.' About goodness it says: 'He commanded the skies above and opened the doors of heaven, and rained down מן on them to eat, and gave them grain of heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now he connects the flood to the מן. He compares the 'openings' of heaven used for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since God's goodness must be larger than His punishment, the מן should have come down in greater amounts than the flood. The verses support this. The flood came through 'windows' (ארובות), while the מן came through 'doors' (דלתות), which are bigger openings.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that מדה טובה is greater than מדת פורענות is a well-known principle that appears in several places in חז״ל.

phrases.english: And which measure is greater,
the measure of goodness or the measure of punishment?
You must say: the measure of goodness is greater
than the measure of punishment.
Regarding the measure of punishment it says:
"And the windows of heaven were opened" (Genesis 7:11).
Regarding the measure of goodness it says:
"He commanded the skies above
and opened the doors of heaven
and rained down manna upon them to eat
and gave them grain of heaven" (Psalms 78:23–24).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֵי זֶה מִדָּה מְרוּבָּה, מִדָּה טוֹבָה אוֹ מִדַּת פּוּרְעָנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the flood measurement from step 14 and builds a comparison to the מן.
steps.raayaObject: That the מן fell in greater amounts than the flood waters
steps.raayaSupportSource: Genesis 7:11 (windows of heaven) compared with Psalms 78:23–24 (doors of heaven)

steps.title: The calculation: the manna was sixty cubits high
steps.stepSummary: A door equals four windows. Two doors make eight windows, four times the flood's two windows. So the מן was 4 × 15 = 60 אמות high.
steps.simpleTranslation: How many windows fit in a door? Four. Four for each door makes eight. So it turns out that the מן that fell for ישראל was sixty אמות high.
steps.whatsHappening: He finishes the math and arrives back at his original claim of sixty אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Windows' (plural) means at least two windows, and they produced fifteen אמות of water. 'Doors' (plural) means two doors, and each door is the size of four windows, so together they equal eight windows. That is four times the flood's opening, so 4 × 15 = 60 אמות.
steps.whatToRemember: The sixty אמות come from a simple ratio. The flood came through two windows and rose fifteen אמות above the mountains. The מן came through two doors, which equal eight windows, so it was four times as much: sixty אמות. This shows God's goodness is greater than His punishment.

phrases.english: How many windows are in a door?
Four, and four for the second door,
which makes eight,
and it turns out that the manna that fell for Israel
was sixty cubits high.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִמְצָא מָן שֶׁיָּרַד לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל גָּבוֹהַּ שִׁשִּׁים אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the windows-versus-doors comparison of step 15 into a number, proving the claim of step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מן was sixty אמות high: four times the fifteen אמות of the flood, because the 'doors of heaven' equal four times the 'windows of heaven.'

steps.title: A ברייתא: the manna piled so high that kings everywhere saw it
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן יהודה teaches that the מן piled up so high that all the kings of East and West could see it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: איסי בן יהודה says: the מן that fell for ישראל would pile up and rise until all the kings of East and West could see it, as it says: 'You prepare a table before me in front of my enemies... my cup overflows.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that also describes the מן as piling up very high. This backs up the huge height from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר המודעי said the מן was 60 אמות high. איסי בן יהודה agrees that the מן was enormous, high enough for kings far away to see. The verse 'a table before me in front of my enemies' means that God fed ישראל in a way their enemies could see.

phrases.english: It was taught: Isi ben Yehuda says:
The manna that fell for the Jewish people
would pile up and rise
until they could see it,
all the kings of the East and the West,
as it says: 'You prepare a table before me'
'in front of my enemies... my cup overflows.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the great height of the מן described in step 16
steps.raayaObject: That the מן piled up to a huge height
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of איסי בן יהודה, based on תהלים כג:ה

steps.title: אביי: דוד's cup in the עולם הבא holds 221 לוג
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from the word רויה, through its גימטריא, that דוד's cup in the עולם הבא holds 221 לוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: learn from this that דוד's cup in the עולם הבא holds 221 לוג, as it says 'my cup overflows (רויה).' The word רויה equals that number in גימטריא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side teaching. אביי takes the end of the verse just quoted and uses it to teach something about the עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of רויה add up to 221: ר is 200, ו is 6, י is 10, and ה is 5. So דוד's cup, which 'overflows,' holds 221 לוג. This does not move the מן discussion forward. It is a short aside that grows out of the same verse.

keyTerms.meaning: a לוג (a measure of liquid volume)
the number value of the letters in a word

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from this
that the cup of David in the World to Come
holds two hundred twenty-one log,
as it says: 'My cup overflows (revaya),'
and revaya in gematria comes out to that.
phrases.notes: ר=200, ו=6, י=10, ה=5, which totals 221

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching taken from the verse quoted in step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's cup in the World to Come holds 221 לוג, the גימטריא of רויה

steps.title: The flood and the manna are not comparable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר המודעי's math. The flood fell over forty days and covered the whole world, while the מן fell in one hour and only for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these are not alike! There, the flood came over forty days, while here the מן fell in one hour. There, it covered the whole world, while here it was for ישראל alone. So they should have had much more than 60 אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי אלעזר המודעי's calculation from step 16 and attacks it. It says the flood and the מן cannot be measured against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases differ in time (forty days versus one hour) and in area (the whole world versus only ישראל's camp). If the 'doors' of the מן really let through four times as much as the flood's 'windows,' the pile over such a small area should have been far higher than 60 אמות. So the simple comparison does not add up.

phrases.english: But this is not comparable.
There (the flood) was over forty days,
here (the manna) was one hour.
There it was for the whole world,
here it was for the Jewish people alone,
so they should have had much more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the 60 אמות calculation in step 16 and challenges it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The time and the area are so different that the flood cannot be used to measure the מן. By his own logic, the מן should have been far higher.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר המודעי learned it from a גזרה שוה of 'opening'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר המודעי was not doing physical math. He learned a גזירה שוה from the word 'opening' in both verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר המודעי learned 'opening' from 'opening.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי אלעזר המודעי's comparison is based on a word that appears in both verses, not on measuring time and area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flood verse says the windows of heaven 'were opened' (נפתחו), and the מן verse says God 'opened' (פתח) the doors of heaven. Because the same root appears in both, he links the two cases with a גזירה שוה and compares them directly. The differences in time and area therefore do not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: he learned it (through a word comparison)
a teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two places

steps.whatToRemember: The 60 אמות figure is based on a גזירה שוה ('opening' and 'opening'), not on physical calculation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i
derived 'opening' from 'opening.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the comparison rests on a textual source (a גזירה שוה), not on physical measurement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think he was making a physical calculation, so the differences in time and area would undo it
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'opening' in both verses links them, so the comparison works no matter how the two cases differ physically

steps.title: Where do the five עינויים of יום הכיפורים come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה ('forbidden to eat') and asks what the five עינויים correspond to in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'It is forbidden to eat.' What do these five עינויים correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: This opens a new topic. The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה about יום הכיפורים and asks for a hint in the Torah for the five types of עינוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah only says 'you shall afflict yourselves.' The גמרא wants to know why the משנה forbids these specific categories. It looks for something in the Torah that matches the number five.

keyTerms.meaning: forbidden to eat (the opening words of the משנה)

phrases.english: 'It is forbidden to eat.'
These five afflictions, what do they correspond to?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה. הָנֵי חֲמִשָּׁה עִנּוּיִין כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מן topic and returns to the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah hint for the five עינויים

steps.title: רב חסדא: five mentions of עינוי in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the five עינויים match the five places where the Torah mentions afflicting oneself on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: they match the five times the Torah mentions עינוי: 'And on the tenth,' 'But on the tenth,' 'a שבת שבתון,' 'a שבת שבתון,' and 'It shall be for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. He lists five verses, and each one includes the command 'you shall afflict yourselves.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each verse is named by its opening words: במדבר כט:ז, ויקרא כג:כז, ויקרא כג:לב, ויקרא טז:לא, and ויקרא טז:כט. Five separate mentions of עינוי hint at five categories of עינוי.

keyTerms.meaning: and it shall be for you

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
They correspond to the five afflictions in the Torah:
'And on the tenth,' and 'But on the tenth,'
'A Shabbat of complete rest,' and 'A Shabbat of complete rest,'
and 'It shall be for you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה עִנּוּיִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Five Torah verses that mention עינוי match the five categories

steps.title: But the משנה lists six, not five
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה lists six prohibitions, so how can there be only five?
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these five? We learned six in the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's count. The משנה lists eating, drinking, washing, anointing, wearing shoes, and marital relations, which is six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five verses only fit if there are five categories. Since the משנה names six items, the match seems to fall apart.

phrases.english: Are these five?
But we learned six!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי חֲמִשָּׁה הָווּ? וַאֲנַן שִׁיתָּא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count in step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The match between five verses and the prohibitions in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists six items, which does not match five verses.

steps.title: Drinking is included in eating
steps.stepSummary: Drinking counts as part of eating, so the six items are really five categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: Drinking is included in eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that eating and drinking together make up one category of עינוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once drinking is grouped under eating, the six items in the משנה become five categories. That matches רב חסדא's five verses.
steps.confusionAlert: Drinking is still forbidden on יום הכיפורים. It is simply counted inside the category of eating, not as a separate category.

phrases.english: Drinking is included in eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Regroups the items so that two of them form one category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating and drinking are two separate categories, which makes six
steps.terutzMaskana: Drinking falls under eating, which makes five categories

steps.title: ריש לקיש's proof: the Torah calls drinking wine 'eating'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש proves that drinking counts as eating, because the Torah says 'you shall eat' about מעשר of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: As ריש לקיש said: from where do we know that drinking is included in eating? As it says: 'And you shall eat before ה׳ your God the מעשר of your grain, your wine, and your oil.' תירוש is wine, and the verse still calls it 'you shall eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up the answer that drinking is part of eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses the word 'eat' for consuming תירוש, which is wine, a drink. This shows that the Torah's word 'eating' can include drinking. So the two count as one category of עינוי.
steps.whatToRemember: The five עינויים match five verses. The משנה's six items are five categories, because drinking is part of eating. ריש לקיש tries to prove this from the verse about תירוש, but the next step rejects that proof, and step 28 brings a new one.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that drinking falls under 'eating' in the language of the תורה also matters in other areas of הלכה that discuss eating.

phrases.english: As Reish Lakish said:
From where do we know that drinking is included in eating?
As it says: 'And you shall eat before the Lord your God'
'the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your oil.'
Tirosh is wine,
and the verse calls it 'and you shall eat.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מִנַּיִן לִשְׁתִיָּה שֶׁהִיא בִּכְלַל אֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the answer given in step 24
steps.raayaObject: That drinking is included in eating
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים יד:כג, where wine is described with the word 'you shall eat'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש's proposed source that drinking is part of eating. The proof is rejected in step 26 and replaced in step 28.

steps.title: Maybe the wine was eaten inside a sauce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects ריש לקיש's proof: the wine in his verse might have been eaten as part of a sauce called אניגרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe he ate the wine as part of an אניגרון sauce!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on ריש לקיש's proof from the last step. It says the verse's word 'eat' might mean wine that was actually eaten, mixed into food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש assumed that 'eating' wine must mean drinking it. The גמרא shows another possibility: wine can be mixed into a dish and truly eaten. If so, the verse says nothing about drinking, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do you know)? A phrase used to question an assumption
But perhaps; introduces another possible reading
A sauce or dish with wine mixed in, which is eaten rather than drunk

phrases.english: From where do you know? Perhaps he ate it
by means of anigron (a sauce with wine mixed in)!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? וְדִילְמָא דְּאַכְלֵיהּ עַל יְדֵי אֲנִיגְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of ריש לקיש from step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects ריש לקיש's verse as a proof that drinking counts as eating.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse may refer to wine that is literally eaten as part of a dish, not wine that is drunk.

steps.title: רבה בר שמואל defines the wine sauces
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל explains what אניגרון and אכסיגרון are, which shows that wine really can be eaten inside food.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר שמואל said: אניגרון is beet juice (mixed with wine). אכסיגרון is the water of all boiled vegetables (mixed with wine).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection by quoting רבה בר שמואל, who explains what these wine dishes are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This definition shows that אניגרון is a real, known dish, so the rejection in step 26 is not just a guess. Because wine is mixed with vegetable liquids, a person eats the wine as part of a cooked food.

keyTerms.meaning: A dish made from the water of boiled vegetables (with wine)

phrases.english: As Rabba bar Shmuel said:
Anigron is beet juice (mixed with wine),
akhsigron is the water of all boiled vegetables (mixed with wine).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 26 by defining אניגרון.
steps.raayaObject: That wine can really be eaten as part of a dish.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רבה בר שמואל defining אניגרון and אכסיגרון.

steps.title: A new proof from strong drink bought with מעשר שני money
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב brings a new verse: the תורה tells us to spend מעשר שני money on שכר, strong drink, and still says 'you shall eat'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא בר יעקב said: the proof is from here: 'And you shall spend the money on whatever your soul desires, on cattle, sheep, wine, and strong drink.' Strong drink is a drink, yet the תורה calls having it 'and you shall eat'.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a new proof from a different verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שכר is clearly a beverage, so it is normally drunk. The same verse goes on to say 'and you shall eat'. That would show the תורה counts drinking as a kind of eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier approach and offers a new one
From here, meaning from this verse
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: (the proof is) from here:
"And you shall give the money for whatever
your soul desires, for cattle and for sheep,
for wine and for strong drink."
Strong drink is a drink,
and the Merciful One calls it "and you shall eat."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof of ריש לקיש with a new verse.
steps.raayaObject: That drinking is included in the תורה's idea of eating.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מעשר שני verse that lists שכר and then says 'and you shall eat'.

steps.title: The same sauce objection against the new proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the same rejection: maybe this strong drink was also eaten inside an אניגרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe here too he ate it as part of an אניגרון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new proof with the same objection it used before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שכר was mixed into a sauce and eaten, then 'and you shall eat' means real eating. In that case, this verse also proves nothing about drinking.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; applies the same reasoning to a new case

phrases.english: From where do you know? Perhaps here too
he ate it by means of anigron!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? וְדִילְמָא הָכָא נָמֵי דְּאַכְלֵיהּ עַל יְדֵי אֲנִיגְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the step 26 objection against רב אחא בר יעקב's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Challenges רב אחא בר יעקב's proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The שכר might have been eaten inside a dish rather than drunk.

steps.title: שכר means something that makes you drunk
steps.stepSummary: The proof is defended: the verse says שכר, which means a drink that intoxicates. A drink mixed into a sauce does not make a person drunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse writes 'שכר', meaning something that makes a person drunk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection and saves רב אחא בר יעקב's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שכר comes from 'getting drunk'. Wine mixed into an אניגרון no longer makes people drunk. So the verse must be talking about the drink in its normal drinkable form, and the תורה still calls it 'eating'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written, meaning the verse uses this word

phrases.english: "Strong drink" is written,
(meaning) something that intoxicates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the verse's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שכר could have been eaten mixed into a sauce.
steps.terutzMaskana: שכר means something intoxicating. A mixture does not intoxicate, so the verse refers to the drink in its drinkable form.

steps.title: Maybe שכר is an intoxicating food like a fig
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe שכר in the verse is not a drink at all, but a food that intoxicates, like a sweet dried fig from קעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it means a pressed fig from קעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from the last step. Some foods can also make a person drunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depended on 'intoxicating' meaning a drink. If a food like דבילה קעילית can intoxicate, then שכר might mean that food. Then 'and you shall eat' is plain eating, and the proof is lost again.

keyTerms.meaning: A cake of pressed dried figs
From the town of Keilah, known for sweet, strong figs

phrases.english: But perhaps (it means) a pressed fig from Keilah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שכר must mean an intoxicating drink.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some foods also intoxicate, so 'something that intoxicates' could be a food that is really eaten.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying figs are a drink. It is asking whether the word שכר could mean any intoxicating thing, including a food.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows a fig can make a person drunk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא about a כהן who ate a fig from קעילה or drank honey or milk and then entered the מקדש. This shows such foods can intoxicate.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If he ate a pressed fig from קעילה, or drank honey and milk, and entered the מקדש...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its challenge with a ברייתא. The quote continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא talks about a כהן who becomes affected by a קעילה fig before serving in the מקדש. That shows חז״ל treated this fig as something that can intoxicate. This supports the idea that שכר could mean a food.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught: If he ate a pressed fig from Keilah
or drank honey or milk
and entered the Temple —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge in step 31.
steps.raayaObject: That a דבילה קעילית can intoxicate.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a כהן entering the מקדש after eating such a fig. The ruling continues on the next עמוד.
